reasoning: Multiple independent polls consistently show Tisza leading Fidesz by 8-12 percentage points among decided voters (around 47-50% vs 38-39%). However, several factors favor Fidesz: 1) Hungary's electoral system with 106 single-member constituencies rewards larger parties and rural strongholds where Fidesz is stronger; 2) The opposition needs a 3-5 point national lead just to win due to gerrymandering; 3) ~20% remain undecided; 4) Pro-government pollsters show Fidesz leading; 5) Orbán has never lost a national election and controls state institutions. Despite Tisza's polling lead, the structural advantages and historical precedent suggest this remains competitive.
